hero.headline: Scan Memory. Hook Functions. Build the Cheat.
hero.description: A hands-on competition for building trainers, mods, and exploits on purpose-built game targets. No real online games, no bans — just sandboxed binaries, raw memory, and your tools.

categories.name: Memory Scanning
categories.description: Locate health, ammo, position, and other game state values in live process memory.

categories.name: Pointer Research
categories.description: Build stable multi-level pointer chains that survive game restarts and level loads.

categories.name: Code Injection
categories.description: Write and inject DLLs into the game process. Hook functions and redirect execution.

categories.name: Function Hooking
categories.description: Intercept game functions — damage, movement, rendering — to read, modify, or block them.

categories.name: Speedrun Exploits
categories.description: Find wrong warps, out-of-bounds skips, and logic bypasses to complete levels in record time.

categories.name: Mod Development
categories.description: Create gameplay modifications: new items, custom maps, altered game rules, and visual hacks.

schedule.event: Competition opens — game binaries and VM images released
Opening stream — tool walkthrough and warmup challenge
Award stream — top team demos and technique breakdowns

faq.a: No. All targets are purpose-built game binaries or open-source games provided specifically for this event. Using cheats on real commercial games is strictly prohibited.
Cheat Engine, x64dbg, ReClass.NET, and a C++ compiler for DLL injection. The lab VM has everything pre-installed. External tools are allowed as long as they run on the lab machine.

faq.q: Do I need game development experience?
faq.a: No — but familiarity with memory concepts (pointers, offsets, heap vs stack) helps a lot. The warmup challenge is designed to get you started from scratch.
Each challenge reveals a flag in CHEAT{...} format when the objective is completed — for example, the target value is set to the flag string once your cheat activates correctly.

lab.title: Cheat Challenges
lab.subtitle: Sandboxed game targets
lab.description: Counter-Strike 2 desparately need to improve the VAC Anti-cheat system, hackers please try your best to develop mods to bypass it, so that the company can improve. All game binaries below run in this provided Windows machine. Do not run them outside of this CTF. Each challenge is self-contained and will be examined by the refrees later if the objective is met. Go deep down layers under the OS to avoid detection from the game's anti-cheat. Work through them in order — later challenges build on skills from earlier ones.

questions.title: Skin Changer
questions.description: Write a program to allow players to change to any skins they want. Note: do not get caught by the anti-cheat system

questions.title: Full-on Hack Mode
questions.description: Write a program to allow users to cheat with aimbot or wall seethrough. Note: do not get caught by the anti-cheat system

allowed: Use Cheat Engine, x64dbg, ReClass.NET, IDA, Ghidra, or any tool that runs in the lab VM
Write and inject DLLs into the provided game processes
Modify game memory, patch binaries, and hook functions at runtime
Reverse and modify game asset files (maps, configs, data files)
Use speedrun techniques including out-of-bounds and logic exploits on provided targets
not_allowed: Use any cheat or exploit in real commercial multiplayer games
Target any game binary not on the provided list
Share working cheat code or DLLs publicly during the competition
Distribute copyrighted game assets or binaries outside the lab VM
Attack competition infrastructure or other participants
